site.tagline: Precision astronomy & orbit analysis libraries for embedded and research systems
site.description: Siderust builds mission-critical astronomical computation and physical modeling libraries in pure Rust. From embedded spacecraft flight software to research-grade pipelines, validated against authoritative ephemerides, zero unsafe code, zero hidden allocations.
site.mission: Siderust aims to be the reference ephemeris and orbit‑analysis library for embedded flight‑software as well as research‐grade pipelines. Every algorithm ships with validation tests against authoritative data (JPL Horizons, IMCCE, SOFA). No unsafe blocks, no hidden allocations.
values: Correctness first: every algorithm validated against JPL Horizons, IMCCE, and SOFA
Zero unsafe code and zero hidden allocations; suitable for bare-metal and real-time systems
Type-level guarantees: reference frames and units encoded in the type system
Reproducible science: deterministic builds and comprehensive benchmarks

home.benchmarkLink: See benchmarks: up to 14× faster than ERFA →
home.performanceFirstDesc: Zero-cost abstractions and SIMD optimizations where it counts. Built for speed without sacrificing safety.
home.typeSafeDesc: Leverage Rust's powerful type system for compile-time guarantees and fearless refactoring.
home.wellDocumentedDesc: Comprehensive documentation with examples. We believe great docs are as important as great code.
home.featuredProjectsDesc: Our most popular and actively maintained libraries.
home.readyToStartDesc: Check out our projects, browse the documentation, or contribute to make Rust development even better.
home.supportDesc: Sponsorship keeps our open-source maintenance steady and helps us deliver roadmap improvements with dependable responsiveness.

about.title: About {name}

about.serveSpacecraft: Spacecraft engineers building autonomous navigation and guidance systems
about.serveObservatory: Observatory operators planning observations and tracking celestial targets
about.serveResearchers: Researchers requiring reproducible, validated astronomical computations

about.whatWeBuildIntro: Our libraries provide mission-critical astronomical computation with an uncompromising focus on:
about.buildValidationDesc: Every algorithm tested against JPL Horizons, IMCCE, and SOFA authoritative ephemerides with published accuracy metrics
about.buildSafetyDesc: Zero unsafe blocks, zero hidden allocations. Suitable for bare-metal embedded systems and real-time flight software
about.buildTypesDesc: Reference frames (ICRS, Ecliptic, Topocentric), coordinate centers (Helio, Geo, Bary), and physical units encoded in types; impossible states don't compile
about.buildReproDesc: Deterministic builds, pinned algorithm versions, comprehensive benchmarks, and no platform-dependent behavior
about.buildPerfDesc: SIMD auto-vectorization, zero-cost abstractions, and optimized numerical kernels (VSOP87, ELP2000) benchmarked at <200ns per evaluation
about.ecoSiderust: Ephemeris and celestial mechanics (VSOP87, ELP2000, DE440, DE-441, Kepler solvers)
about.ecoAffn: Affine transformations with compile-time reference frame safety
about.ecoQtty: Physical quantities with dimensional analysis (Length, Angle, Mass, Time, etc.)
about.contributeIntro: We welcome contributions from everyone! Whether you're fixing a bug, adding a feature, or improving documentation, your help is appreciated.
about.step1Title: Find an issue or create one
about.step1Desc: Browse our GitHub organization for issues labeled "good first issue" or "help wanted".
about.step2Desc: Create your own fork and set up the development environment locally.
about.step3Desc: Work on your changes in a dedicated branch from main.
about.step4Desc: Write clean code, add tests, and update documentation as needed.
about.step5Desc: Open a PR with a clear description. We'll review and provide feedback promptly.
about.guidelineStyle: Follow the existing code style and formatting
about.guidelineDocs: Add doc comments for public APIs
about.guidelineUnsafe: Avoid unsafe code unless absolutely necessary
about.readyToContributeDesc: Check out our open issues and start making an impact today.
about.connectDesc: Have questions or want to get involved? Reach out through our GitHub organization.

demo.title: Interactive Demo
demo.seoDescription: Try Siderust's high-precision astronomy engine live in your browser, sky plots, coordinate transforms, and time conversions powered by WebAssembly.
demo.heroDesc: Explore Siderust's capabilities live in your browser, powered entirely by WebAssembly, no backend required.
demo.loadError: Failed to load the astronomy engine. Please reload the page.
demo.skySphereHint: 3D planetarium view from an observer on Earth's surface. Drag to look around from the center, zoom with the wheel, and compare the target's path with the selected altitude threshold.
demo.skySphereAriaLabel: Interactive 3D planetarium view from an observer on Earth's surface, showing the target's trajectory and altitude threshold over 24 hours.
demo.skyPlotDesc: Track altitude and azimuth of celestial objects over a 24-hour window.
demo.neverRises: Never rises, always below the horizon
demo.noEvents: No crossing events for this configuration.
demo.altChartAriaLabel: Line chart showing altitude versus time for the selected target.
demo.azChartAriaLabel: Line chart showing azimuth versus time for the selected target.
demo.coordsDesc: Transform directions and positions between reference frames using the full IAU model stack.
demo.localHorizontalDesc: Convert a celestial direction to altitude / azimuth for an observer.
demo.posTransformDesc: Retrieve an ephemeris position and convert its center or frame.
demo.timeDesc: Convert between UTC, Julian Date, Modified Julian Date, and explore observation periods.
demo.poweredByDesc: All computations run entirely in your browser using Siderust's WASM engine, no data leaves your machine.
